body:
Cloud condensate that fills only part of a cell is more concentrated within the cloud than in the cell mean, and its particles are larger and fall faster: the 1-moment velocities of cloud liquid (Stokes) and cloud ice (Chen et al., 2022) take the mean particle size from the specific humidity and a prescribed number concentration. This PR adds an option to evaluate these velocities at the in-cloud specific humidity.

## Changes

- New parameter `sgs_cloud_sedimentation_cf_floor` (`c_min`, in `(0, 1]`, default `1`) in `SGSQuadratureParameters`, with a range check at construction.
- With `c_min < 1`, `set_precipitation_velocities!` evaluates the 1M cloud liquid and cloud ice terminal velocities at `q / clamp(CF, c_min, 1)` (`incloud_specific_humidity`). The velocity multiplies the mean condensate, so the sedimentation flux is the in-cloud flux weighted by the cloud fraction.
- Without EDMF, `q` and `CF` are the cell mean and the grid-mean cloud fraction `ᶜcloud_fraction`. With `PrognosticEDMFX`, they are the environment mean and the environment cloud fraction `ᶜcloud_fraction⁰`; the updrafts sediment cloud condensate at their own mean specific humidity.
- The cloud fraction is an explicit precomputed quantity. `set_explicit_precomputed_quantities!` therefore sets the velocities that read it after it has updated the cloud fraction (`sedimentation_reads_cloud_fraction`), so that the cache depends on the state alone, which restarts require. The Newton iterates in between refresh the velocities with the cloud fraction of that update.
- The option affects the state-dependent velocities (`cloud_liquid_terminal_velocity: Stokes`, `cloud_ice_terminal_velocity: Chen2022`); a fixed velocity is independent of the specific humidity.

## Behavior

- The default `c_min = 1` evaluates the velocities at the mean specific humidity through the same code path as on `main`, so results are unchanged and `ref_counter.jl` is untouched.
- With `c_min < 1`, the velocities are computed twice per full cache update: in the implicit part and again after the cloud fraction update.
- The floor bounds the concentration factor by `1 / c_min`. The upper bound on the cloud-ice fall speed itself is part of CloudMicrophysics (`Chen2022_small_ice_terminal_velocity_max`, 1.5 m/s, CliMA/CloudMicrophysics.jl#861, in 0.51.1). Runs with a small `c_min` should use that release; this PR does not depend on it. The Stokes cloud liquid velocity has no upper bound in CloudMicrophysics, so the floor alone limits it.

## Tests

In `test/parameterized_tendencies/microphysics/terminal_velocity.jl`:

- "In-cloud specific humidity": the default and the range check of the parameter, `incloud_specific_humidity` at, above, and below the floor and for negative condensate, and the increase of the Stokes and Chen et al. (2022) fall speeds with decreasing cloud fraction down to the floor.
- "In-cloud velocities through `set_precipitation_velocities!`": with the parameter read from a toml file, `ᶜwₗ` and `ᶜwᵢ` of a 1M column and of a `PrognosticEDMFX` Bomex column equal the terminal velocities at the in-cloud specific humidity, for condensate and a cloud fraction that vary with height. The EDMF case checks that the environment cloud fraction enters and the grid-mean cloud fraction does not.
- "In-cloud velocities through `set_precomputed_quantities!`": a cloud fraction left in the cache before the call does not affect the velocities, for the grid mean and the EDMF environment.

In `test/restart.jl` (Buildkite), the 1M `PrognosticEDMFX` DYCOMS RF01 restart case runs with the Stokes cloud liquid velocity and `sgs_cloud_sedimentation_cf_floor = 0.1` (`toml/cloud_sedimentation_restart_test.toml`).

This is the in-cloud sedimentation part of f5675258356c1fe248e8d6ded3845c664495febf on `ts/swcre-30pct`, ported onto `main` and extended to cloud liquid.
title: Evaluate the 1M cloud condensate terminal velocities at the in-cloud specific humidity

The updraft gets one radius `R` that sets both its form drag and its turbulent entrainment.

**Plume radius.** `R = H √clamp(a, a_lb, a_max)`, with `H = R_d T_sfc,ref / g` and the lower area bound `a_lb = (R_min / H)²` from a minimum radius that grows linearly with height above the surface `R_min(z) = min(c_R (z − z_sfc), R_max)` 

**Form drag.** `d_c = α_d / 2 (1 / R + 1 / R⁰)`, `R⁰ = H √clamp(a⁰, 1 − a_max, 1)`. The floor only weakens the drag of thin updrafts.

**Turbulent entrainment.** `ε_T = c₁ exp(−c₂ a) + 2 c_e √tke / R`: exchange across the plume edge at velocity `c_e √tke` on perimeter `2πR` over area `πR²`, with the same `R` as the drag. Optionally tapered with height by `exp(−((z − z_sfc) / H_t)²)`.

body:
Under SGS quadrature, the 1M microphysics places rain and snow on a subgrid precipitation shaft (`sgs_precip_incloud_fraction`, default 1; width `max(a_p, sgs_precip_fraction_floor)`), but sedimentation used the terminal velocity of the cell mean. This PR makes the grid-mean and environment rain and snow velocities the mass-weighted mean of the velocities in the shaft and in the rest of the cell:

`w_eff = a_s φ_in w(φ_in q) + (1 − a_s) φ_out w(φ_out q)`, with `φ_in = 1 − β_p + β_p/a_s`, `φ_out = 1 − β_p`.

- New `shaft_weighted_terminal_velocity`, `precip_shaft_options`, `on_precip_shaft` in `terminal_velocity_utils.jl`; wired into both 1M `set_precipitation_velocities!` methods. Updraft velocities are unchanged.
- Behavior change for default 1M runs: at the 0.1 floor, rain falls 1.2–1.7x faster and snow ~1.2x faster (Chen 2022).
- Unit tests for the limits, the zone-flux identity, and the floor; RICO EDMF column runs 4 h with zero allocations in `set_precipitation_velocities!`.
title: Sediment 1M rain and snow at the shaft-weighted terminal velocity

body: This PR applies `toml/default_parameters.toml` to every run, between the ClimaParams defaults and the config `toml` files, and exposes its path as `ClimaAtmos.Parameters.DEFAULT_PARAMS_FILEPATH` for ClimaCoupler. Configs that did not list it change results. The configs and tests no longer list it. The coupler will use this API in a followup PR.
title: Provide public default parameter path

body:
Change the default sedimentation velocities for 1M:
- Stokes for cloud liquid
- Chen2022 for cloud ice

We already use Chen2022 for rain and snow.
title: Use Stokes and Chen2022 as default 1M
